clue.text: Film kicks off conflict for second time

indicators.note: conflict stands for, that is replaces, the letter named after it in the word for kicks off

parts.note: kicks off means starts, begins
T is the abbreviation for time, and here the second T of the word is meant
a conflict is a war

explanation.surface: A war breaks out again, this time on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' tells you to swap: STARTS has two Ts, and the second one (T for time) gives way to WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names George Lucas's famous 1977 space-opera movie and its franchise.

clue.text: Old letter-writer stumped university in China

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped, a way of being out

indicators.note: the university letter is placed inside the word for China

parts.note: china (from rhyming slang china plate) means mate, a pal

explanation.surface: Someone was baffled when a university opened in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' hides behind a capital letter: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' = mate, so china = PAL. ST is stumped in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle wrote many of the New Testament epistles, letters to early churches, making him an ancient letter-writer.

clue.text: Goal in marriage? Lying dreadfully, without doubt

indicators.note: the word for goal goes inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union
a goal or aim pursued is a quest

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the letters of lying are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the aim of a marriage is lying shamelessly, and certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark pretends to ask about marriage vows; 'dreadfully' is the anagram signal for 'Lying', whose shuffle ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without hesitation or doubt is doing it in an unquestioning manner, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Giggle about weight? A lot of birds do it

definitions.text: A lot of birds do it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the giggle word goes round the weight letter

parts.note: to giggle is to titter

explanation.surface: A slimmer giggles about their weight, as many birds apparently do.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds chirp and chatter, which is what this verb means; many birds make such sounds together.

clue.text: Country High School's keeping a girl who's succeeded?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the school letters enclose the country

parts.note: HS is the abbreviation for High School, plus the S of the possessive
Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, a country

explanation.surface: A country school takes in a girl who has done well.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's gives a letter here: H(EIRE)S plus S. The definition is cryptic: a girl who succeeds (inherits), not one who triumphs.
explanation.definitionFit: A female who inherits, or succeeds to, an estate or title is so called; the question mark flags the pun on succeeding.

clue.text: Men with guns following alien whale and other things

indicators.note: following places the gunners after the alien and whale pieces

parts.note: ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film, is the classic crossword alien
cete is an old word for a whale, from the Greek, as in cetacean
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

explanation.surface: Armed men hunt an alien whale, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: CETE is an archaic word solvers rarely meet; the Royal Artillery is the usual crossword source of gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase, abbreviated etc., is used to mean and the rest, or and so on.

clue.text: I've to abandon plunge, so went in slowly

indicators.note: the letters of I've are dropped from the word for plunge

parts.note: a plunge or steep drop is a nosedive
taken as written, its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A diver gives up a plunge and enters the water cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' removes IVE from the end of NOSEDIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward cautiously, as a car or boat does, is to move forward by inches, a verb sense.

clue.text: Vote to exclude leader's share

indicators.note: the leading letter of the vote word is excluded

parts.note: a vote is a ballot

explanation.surface: A vote decides to cut the leader's share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exclude leader' drops the B from BALLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out is to apportion or distribute, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Steer idiot to grasp variable contradiction

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
Y is a letter used in algebra for an unknown or variable
an idiot is a moron

explanation.surface: Someone guides a fool towards understanding a changing contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb; it is the animal, OX. MORON grasps Y: MOR(Y)ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech pairing opposites, such as deafening silence, is a self-contradiction in terms.

clue.text: Open front of attic to find fungus

parts.note: open, frank and honest, means candid

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of attic

explanation.surface: Open the front of the attic and you find mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like a verb but is an adjective: candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeast-like fungus genus, one species of which causes thrush infections.

clue.text: Picked up Caribbean island meal?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the island's name is taken by ear

parts.note: Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic

explanation.surface: Someone collects a Caribbean islander's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH TEA is a British early-evening meal of a cooked dish with bread and tea; the question mark admits the pronunciation is approximate.
explanation.definitionFit: This British meal, eaten late afternoon or early evening, usually includes a hot dish and tea.

clue.text: Scramble up mountain track, then maybe stop

indicators.note: scramble means mix up the letters of the following words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Climbers scramble up a mountain path and then perhaps pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scramble' is a climbing word in the surface; here it rearranges UP MOUNTAIN TRACK. 'maybe' says a stop (full stop) is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is one example of the symbols, like commas, used to divide written text.

clue.text: Marshal, gathering support, retreating not far away

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the marshal surrounds the support

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the support word is read in reverse

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A military marshal, gathering reinforcements, pulls back to a close position.
explanation.walkthrough: Ney was Napoleon's 'bravest of the brave'; 'retreating' applies only to the support garment, which then sits inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Close at hand, in the vicinity: the adverb means a short distance off.

clue.text: Part of US welcomes Republican with extremely ghastly plan

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the state encloses the party letter

parts.note: a part of the US is a state

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of ghastly

explanation.surface: An American state hosts a Republican with a dreadful scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: ST(R)ATE, then G and Y, the extremes of ghastly.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-term scheme or method for achieving a goal is a synonym.

clue.text: Closed island, trapping fine gander

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the fine letter goes within

parts.note: closed means shut
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A shut island keeps a fine goose captive.
explanation.walkthrough: SHUFTI is British slang (from Arabic) for a quick look. 'gander' is a look, not a goose, here.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a gander is slang for having a look; this British slang word means the same.

clue.text: Leave convict finally in a state for release

indicators.note: the leave and convict pieces go inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state
to leave is to quit

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of convict

explanation.surface: Leaving a convict in a state for release at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' tempts you to look for a fodder of letters; it is the article A followed by California's short form, holding the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict of not guilty frees, or releases, a defendant from the charge.

clue.text: Crown with about two articles

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A king is crowned with a few items about him.
explanation.walkthrough: W + RE + A + THE: the two articles are 'a' and 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle with a garland, as a victor's head, is to crown it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Spinner runs over hill

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A spin bowler runs over a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cricket, where a spinner bowls; here the spinner is a rotating part.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating blade assembly, as on a helicopter, is a mechanical thing that spins.

clue.text: Hunch, in shed, giving instruction

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so the word in is dropped

parts.note: a hunch is an intuition

explanation.surface: A hunch in a garden shed gives some guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut; it means discard. INTUITION loses IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching, especially paid coaching, is a synonym of instruction.

clue.text: Invader from east that could be obtuse

definitions.meaning: one of the Germanic tribe that came over the North Sea to settle in Britain
an obtuse one is between 90 and 180 degrees

explanation.surface: An eastern invader who might be dim-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: the Germanic settler people, and the geometric figure between two lines.

clue.text: Bet 'A' team will get reserve

parts.note: to lay is to bet, as a bookmaker lays odds
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A gambler wagers that the A team will get the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: LAY + A + SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something by for later use is to reserve it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Leading villain likely to fall?

parts.note: leading means top, foremost
a heavy is a villain or thug in a film

explanation.surface: The chief villain looks likely to fall from grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with too much weight at the upper part is unstable and liable to topple.

clue.text: Noted B29 unescorted, heading north, not straight

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: unescorted means alone
not straight means gay

explanation.surface: A noted bomber flies north alone and off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses ALONE, giving ENOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous B-29 bomber that dropped the atomic bomb on Hiroshima in 1945 bore this name.

clue.text: Worth somehow coming in to rescue radio?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come into the word for rescue

parts.note: to rescue is to save

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of worth are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Something worthwhile comes along to rescue the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortwave radio was the classic way to hear distant stations; 'somehow' shuffles 'Worth', and those letters come inside the rescue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio band of short wavelengths, used for long-distance broadcasting, names a kind of radio.

clue.text: In which to boil southern gold pecan nuts?

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of pecan are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cook asks what to boil Southern gold pecan nuts in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' is part of the food picture but rearranges PECAN into CEPAN: S + AU + CEPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cooking pot with a handle is the usual vessel for boiling food on a hob.

clue.text: Put scoop in drum, spinning in this?

definitions.text: Put scoop in drum, spinning in this?

indicators.note: the scoop word is put into the turned drum word
spinning means turned round, so the drum word is read backwards

parts.note: a butt is a cask or barrel, a drum for liquids
to scoop a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: Laundry is put into a drum and spun in this machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drum' is BUTT, a cask; 'spinning' reverses it to TTUB, and WIN is put in: T(WIN)TUB. The whole clue also describes using the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-style washing machine with two drums, one to wash and one to spin-dry clothes.

clue.text: Men strip, being without new material

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: being without means being outside, so the strip surrounds the new letter

parts.note: the Gaza Strip is a territory on the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Men undress, having nothing new to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, an old sense crosswords love; 'strip' is the Gaza Strip, not undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, stiff, sheer silk or synthetic fabric used for dresses is a kind of material.

clue.text: Driver needs this brown stuff, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells you to go by how the word for brown stuff is spoken

parts.note: khaki is a dull brownish cloth, as in army uniform

explanation.surface: A driver needs brown stuff, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech KHAKI is said 'car-key'.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist needs this item to unlock and start the vehicle.

clue.text: Women in Japan hosting local warrior

indicators.note: hosting means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Women in Japan take in a fighter from the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' shows the run womeN IN JApan. 'local' means native to Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese warrior trained in stealth and espionage, local to the Japan of the clue.

clue.text: Jack is really attractive on the outside

indicators.note: the word for really attractive sits outside the word is

parts.note: hot is slang for very attractive

explanation.surface: Jack is really good-looking on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; it is the verb, as in jack up a car: HO(IS)T.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack something up is to lift or raise it, a verb synonym.
